title: Testing with TypeScript is painful: why test code needs looser types and how shoehorn fixes it
summary: Matt Pocock argues that test code shouldn't be held to the same type strictness as application code. Tests must often pass wrong or partial values, forcing noisy `as any` or `as unknown as X` casts. He introduces shoehorn, a library that makes passing partial or wrong types first-class in tests.

principles.text: Test code doesn't need the same type strictness as application code.
principles.quote: Tests don't need to live up to the same level of strictness as the rest of your application code.

principles.text: A broken type in app code means user-facing bugs; in passing tests it is often just busywork.
principles.quote: If you've got a broken type in your app, that'll likely end up in your users finding a bug.

principles.text: Tests must be able to pass the wrong type to verify a function handles bad input.
principles.quote: Sometimes, your tests will need to test that when a function receives the _wrong_ thing, it behaves in the right way.

principles.text: Double assertions like `as unknown as string` are un-ergonomic for a very common testing need.
principles.quote: This is extremely un-ergonomic - a DOUBLE assertion, just to be able to do something extremely common.

principles.text: Mocking large external types (e.g. express Request) forces repeated casts and imports everywhere.
principles.quote: In this case, you might only care about the `req.body` property. But you still need to pass the entire `Request` type to the function.

principles.text: Provide a first-class API for passing partial/wrong values in tests instead of ad hoc casts.
principles.quote: It gives you a first-class way to pass the wrong type to a function.
